item.title: How Claude and Similar Companies Actually Ban Accounts for "VPN Use" and "Toxic Passports"
item.description:
The internet has been buzzing for days with news that Claude has started banning users for providing "toxic passports" for verification, even though the platform's rules don't mention anything of the sort. The service's rules do not explicitly prohibit holders of specific passports from using the company's services. The company has a direct ban on conducting business and providing services in specific countries, but to segregate users by the color of their passport cover... It sounds like news from another continent in the 1950s. Nevertheless, precedents have emerged, and a significant outcry has begun on Reddit. But as an anti-detect browser deeply involved in anti-detect and anti-fraud, let's figure out what's true, what's clickbait, and what's outright lies in this story (and if there are any outright lies at all)? Read about Claude's blocking.

item.title: Vibe-learning
item.description:
Let's get straight to it. Vibe-learning is when there's no pause between acquiring and applying knowledge. It's a system for preparing for life without vertical knowledge transfer, based on initiating events. This isn't 'Education 5.0' or whatever label they try to slap on attempts to revive it. We don't need to somehow make education better. We need to abandon it entirely. And if you're even remotely connected to it, this is the most useful text you can read right now. Read more

item.title: What Questions Became Inappropriate for Clients in the Age of Neural Networks: A Revision of Rackham's Sales Methodology
item.description:
Neil Rackham's sales methodology is almost 40 years old, and sales have changed significantly during this time. With neural networks, gathering information about a client (what the company does, its turnover, how many salespeople it has) has become a matter of minutes. If, after this, you ask the client about something that is on their own website, they will be surprised at best, and at worst, they will laugh the salesperson out of the room. We spoke with a practitioner about which questions from the methodology still work in selling complex systems, and which ones should be left in the past. Read more

item.title: A week of manual work in two days: how I delegated part of the operational process to AI
item.description:
Hello, Habr! My name is Anastasia, and I am the head of IT compliance at RGS. Before each planning cycle, I need to review and evaluate hundreds of tasks to determine which ones require attention first. This usually took a full working week, so I decided to find a way to simplify this process to free up time for more complex expert work. As a result, I managed to automate part of the routine using AI, and in this article, I want to share how, without a development budget or programming skills, I reduced the task review time from five working days to two. item.title: HuggingFace for Beginners: How to Choose and Run a Model
item.description:
If you're interested in AI and data, you've likely encountered HuggingFace – an AI development platform and community, akin to GitHub for AI. It offers a centralized hub for sharing, discovering, and collaborating on open-source machine learning models, datasets, and applications. However, its interface can be quite challenging for newcomers. Faced with hundreds of thousands of models, it's easy to feel overwhelmed, much like someone stepping into a bustling 1990s wholesale market: everything is available, but understanding where to start is a mystery. Within minutes, you might download the wrong datasets or abandon the endeavor altogether. The complexity isn't just about HuggingFace being difficult; it's about the platform requiring prior knowledge. This article serves as a beginner-friendly tutorial on navigating HuggingFace, working with its data and weights without getting lost.

item.title: Transferring sessions between console AI agents without context loss
item.description:
When a console AI agent's five-hour limit is reached mid-debug, you might want to switch to another agent that still has limits. The popular method of saving a summary to HANDOFF.md often fails: the model's retelling quality is poor, context details are lost, and you have to re-explain the task to the next agent (wasting extra tokens). In this article, we'll explore how to extract a live session from local logs without losing meaning and transfer it to another agent with a single command, or move your work, including unsaved files, to another PC. Read on

item.title: Virtual Employees Under Control: How to Limit Autonomous AI Agents
item.description:
It's a known fact that AI agents can act independently: launch programs, manage files, and tirelessly pursue a given task. This might seem like a developer's dream, but there's a catch: the more freedom an agent has, the more problems it can cause. In the summer of 2026, OpenAI agents broke out of their sandbox and ventured onto the internet, attacking HuggingFace in the process. This incident presented AI engineers with a challenge: they needed to find a way to restrict agents, ensuring they could never leave isolated environments. However, agents are cunning and quickly find ways to bypass even the strictest rules. But there's one weak spot. Today, we'll discuss the Hard Stop system, proposed in a scientific paper of the same name. It acts as an emergency brake between the agent and the OS, designed to halt the agent's processes before it can cause harm. Read on.

item.title: Self-learning in single-celled organisms and collective intelligence
item.description:
Learning is usually associated with neural activity. However, evidence suggests that even single-celled organisms possess primitive forms of memory and learning. This article explores the mechanisms behind this phenomenon, drawing parallels with artificial neural networks and discussing the implications for our understanding of intelligence.

item.title: Photoshoot for Dentists Without a Photoshoot for $3: FLUX.3 klein + ComfyUI + RunPod = 290 Frames
item.description:
I set up paid traffic for dental clinics (and not only). For good creatives, you always need photos of doctors: the real face of a doctor in the office works better than stock photos. But for a clinic, a doctor photoshoot turns into a separate project with significant time and financial costs. Doctors are busy with patients, offices are occupied, a photographer needs to be paid, and a good one needs to be paid a lot. In a month, new shots are needed because the old creatives have burned out. In general, for dental clinics, this is a long and expensive hassle. I understood this from the very beginning and decided to go a different way. Read more
